title: Distinct in Every Window

statement.markdown:
Given an integer array `nums` and a window size `k`, return an array where entry `i` is the number of **distinct** values in the window `nums[i .. i+k-1]`.

If `k` is 0 or larger than the array, return an empty array.

Recomputing each window from scratch is O(n·k). Slide instead: what changes when the window moves one step right?

hints: Keep a count map for the current window. Moving right adds one element and removes one.
Distinct count changes only when an added value's count becomes 1, or a removed value's count becomes 0.
Delete map entries when their count hits 0 so the map size IS the distinct count.
solutionExplanation: Classic sliding window with a count map. Each step adds the entering element and (once the window is full) evicts the leaving one; deleting zero-count keys keeps the map's size equal to the distinct count, so each window is answered in O(1). Time O(n), space O(k).
